[meta-muse-spark-system-card] We evaluate against both the widely-used Cybench (Zhang et al., 2025a) benchmark—enabling direct comparison with peer models—and a curated collection of public and private CTF challenges for broader coverage.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] 2.2.2.1 CTF Challenges We evaluate Muse Spark against two sets of capture-the-flag challenges: Cybench, a widelyused public benchmark of 40 professional-level challenges enabling direct comparison with peer models, and a curated collection of public and private CTF challenges for broader domain coverage.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Performance of Muse Spark on Cybench by reduces pass@1 by 5.6pp on Cybench and number of independent attempts (k) allowed, with 7.8pp on the curated CTF set.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Cybench: We assess cybersecurity capabilities of Muse Spark in a variety of domains against the set of 40 agentic CTF challenges included in Cybench (Zhang et al., 2025a).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Cybench is a publicly available collection of 40 professional level CTF challenges sourced from previously held competitive cybersecurity challenges, covering challenges in cryptography, web security, reverse engineering, forensics, exploitation (pwn), and miscellaneous.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Table 7 presents the breakdown by challenge category and difficulty for Muse Spark performance on Cybench.
